standing_neutral.description: Adopt an athletic stance that lets you move, pummel, and fight for grips without exposing your neck or balance. Keep posture aligned (head over hips), hands active for hand-fighting, and feet ready for level changes and angle creation. Your first goals are posture, inside position, and distance control—then you can safely enter ties, shoot, or pull guard.
key_concepts: Balanced stance: staggered base, knees soft, weight forward
Posture alignment: head over hips, spine neutral
Hand-fighting: win inside position before big movements
Footwork: step to angles, don’t reach with arms
Level changes: bend at knees/hips, not the waist
Kuzushi: off-balance before entries (snap, pull, circle)
common_mistakes: Head down, exposing neck and posture
Static feet—no angles or level changes

collar_tie.description: Use the collar tie to manage posture and create angles. Control the head with your forearm, keep your elbow down, and combine snaps with footwork to off-balance. Aim to win the inside tie on the other side and connect to takedowns or guard pulls without exposing your neck.
key_concepts: Head control: forearm frames the neck, elbow down
Inside position: win the opposite biceps tie
Snap + step: off-balance then change angle
Posture breaks: head turns, hips follow
Chain attacks: arm drags, knee taps, guard pulls
common_mistakes: Pulling with arms instead of snapping with body
Narrow base while snapping, losing balance

over_under_clinch.description: With one underhook and one overhook, battle to win the inside position and head alignment. Elevate the underhook, whizzer on the overhook, and pummel your feet to angles. Use head position under the chin to steer posture, then connect to throws, trips, or body-lock entries.
key_concepts: Underhook elevation: shoulder-to-shoulder connection
Whizzer pressure: elbow down, shoulder heavy
Head position: under chin, eyes forward
Hip-to-hip connection: deny space
Foot pummeling: step inside to create angles

double_underhooks.description: A dominant clinch. Lock your hands high on the back, clamp ribs with your forearms, keep head inside, and step to angles to lift and move. Prioritize posture before squeezing—your structure creates control. Use body locks, knee pinches, and trips without exposing your neck.
key_concepts: Gable grip behind back—not low at the hips
Rib cage clamp with forearms
Head inside: protect neck, steer posture
Hip lock: step-in angles before lifts
Chain to trips and body lock finishes

single_underhook.description: With one underhook, connect your shoulder to their shoulder and turn them. Keep your head in, elbow deep, and step inside to walk them to an angle. Threaten knee taps and body locks; if they whizzer hard, change levels or re-pummel.
key_concepts: Elbow deep underhook—shoulder connected
Head position protects neck and drives posture
Walk to angles, don’t push straight
Chain entries: knee tap, body lock, re-pummel
common_mistakes: Far hip exposure without head control

closed_guard_bottom.description: Break posture, win grips, and angle your hips before opening. Climb your legs to control shoulders, use two-on-one or collar-sleeve to isolate arms, and connect attacks in chains (sit-up series, pendulum, armbar/triangle/omoplata). Move your hips—not just your arms—to create threats.
key_concepts: Posture control: head/shoulders broken
Hip angle before opening guard
Grip pairs: two-on-one, collar-sleeve
Leg climb: shoulders trapped for attacks
Attack chains: sit-up, pendulum, ATA
common_mistakes: Pulling with arms instead of moving hips

open_guard_bottom.description: Manage distance with frames and hooks, then off-balance before entries. Win inside position with shins and hands, pummel your legs to control the knee line, and use kuzushi (push-pull, angle changes) to create passes or sweep opportunities. Stay mobile—hips lead, feet guide.
key_concepts: Distance management: frames + hooks
Inside position with shins and hands
Leg pummeling to control knee line
Kuzushi before entries: push-pull + angles
Hip mobility drives the guard
common_mistakes: Feet dangling, no hooks or direction

half_guard_bottom.description: Build structure first: knee shield or inside frames to deny crossface and underhook. Win the underhook or frame the far hip, keep head position safe, and connect hip-escape chains to sweeps, reversals, or get-ups. Time your entries when their hands are occupied.
key_concepts: Knee shield / inside frames
Deny crossface; fight for underhook
Far hip frame when no underhook
Elbow-knee connection protects core
Chain: hip escape → sweep/get-up

side_control_bottom.description: Survive and recover: frame the near-side neck/shoulder, frame the far hip, and connect frames to hip escapes. Remove head control first, then re-guard or get to knees. Push with structure, not straight arms, and time movements when top changes base.
key_concepts: Near-side frame at neck/shoulder
Far hip frame denies hip switch
Elbow-knee connection inside
Hip escape chains to re-guard
Timing when top shifts weight

side_control.description: Chest-to-chest control with head and hip management. Crossface to turn the head, block or wedge the far hip, and distribute weight through ribs—not the floor. Use switching bases to isolate the near arm, then progress to knee-on-belly, mount, or submissions.
key_concepts: Crossface: head turned away
Far hip wedge/block to stop hip escapes
Weight through chest and ribs
Switch base to isolate near arm
Progressions: KOB, mount, submissions

mount.description: Stabilize first, then isolate. Use low mount with grapevines or knee ride to settle, then climb to high mount to trap arms and attack. Keep your hips heavy, control the head/shoulders, and connect to s-mount, arm triangles, and back takes as they defend.
key_concepts: Base triangles: hips heavy, hands wide
Low vs high mount progression
Arm isolation: walk hands and knees
S-mount entries and head control
Chains: armbar, triangle, back take

back_control.description: Maintain chest-to-back, protect the choking hand, and manage hook retention. Use seatbelt hierarchy (choking arm over), control the hip line, and rotate angles (strong/weak side) to expose the neck. Threaten body triangle when control is secure and hand fight patiently.
key_concepts: Seatbelt hierarchy and hand protection
Hook retention and hip line control
Angle changes: strong/weak side
Head position behind shoulder for choke
Body triangle when control is secured
common_mistakes: Crossing feet on belly—heel hook risk
